analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia, 20 November 2026
key_insights: US equities ended near session lows on Thursday: S&P 500 -2.02%, Dow -2.19%, Nasdaq -2.25%. S&P 500 breadth was the worst of the year to date and negative for a fourth straight session.
The AI trade reversed earlier strength, with semiconductors, neoclouds and memory lower. AMZN, SPCX and GOOGL were the weakest large-cap tech names.

The risk-off move followed the ANT (Anthropic) IPO, which opened almost 40% above the $83 IPO price and then fell nearly 20% from the opening tick. Other drivers cited: volatility near 28, higher oil on reports Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran, poorly received retail earnings, hawkish Fedspeak and rising odds of a government shutdown.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, above the $70-78 marketed range, selling 980M shares versus 825M planned and raising $81.3B, the largest listing on record and ahead of SpaceX's $75B. Shares briefly implied a valuation above $2T before paring to about $95.

Some analysts said strong IPO demand is not an all-clear for debt-heavy neoclouds and lower-tier AI infrastructure. Bloomberg also flagged signs that capital rotated out of megacap AI incumbents, possibly to fund Anthropic positions after tight allocations left institutions underweight.
Treasuries firmed with a bull steepening and yields down 1-4 bp. Gold fell 1.5% and WTI settled up 0.5%.

Philly Fed manufacturing fell to +6.3 against a +20.0 consensus and +20.9 in October, the lowest since May. New orders declined for a fourth straight month. Initial claims rose to 203K (consensus 197K) and continuing claims to 1,763K (consensus 1,710K), the highest since late August.

Fed officials stayed hawkish. Goolsbee said inflation is well above target and tariff-driven inflation cannot be looked through if it persists. Bowman estimated AI accounts for 25% of excess inflation. Jefferson said the AI investment boom is adding to near-term inflation. Barr said policy adjustments are still necessary.
The NY Times reported Trump is weighing another round of extensive strikes on Iran. Iran has stepped up military activity in the Strait of Hormuz since the midterm elections.
Nvidia's recruiter approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as part of a search for Jensen Huang's successor. Nvidia confirmed on its earnings call that it does not intend to reinstate Huang.

US stock movers: PANW +6.4% on a beat-and-raise and the $4.5B Applied Compute acquisition. AMD -7.7% after a Hunterbrook short report alleging a blacklisted Chinese firm kept receiving newer AMD firmware. WMT modestly beat in Q3 and raised FY27 guidance.
European equities fell: Germany -1.06%, France -0.81%, UK -0.93%. The FTSE 100 closed at a six-week low. Gilt 10-year yields rose 5 bp while Bund and OAT yields were flat.

ECB labor cost index rose to 3.5% y/y in Q3 from 3.1%, supporting a December hike. Markets price more than a 90% chance of a December hike, with two more possible next year. Reuters reports the ECB will discuss raising the minimum reserve requirement from 1% to 2% next week, saving at least 4.4B euros a year.

BoE Governor Bailey expects inflation to peak below the BoE's 4.9% forecast as energy prices ease, but still expects inflation to accelerate into early 2027. Sterling hit a one-year low below $1.3150 as near-term hike bets eased.

UniCredit and the German government resolved the main political obstacles to UniCredit's Commerzbank takeover. Germany dropped its demand for two supervisory board seats. The government's residual 13.3% stake is unresolved.
FT argued the Shenzhen Trump-Xi-Putin summit left Europe's interests unaddressed. ASML is exposed to a possible US bill extending export controls to DUV immersion tools and services.

Asian equities were mostly lower. Hong Kong fell to its twice-held, year-long support line, led lower by IT and internet stocks, and Taiwan's Taiex fell most. Japan rose 0.71% and India 1.14%. Tencent fell 6.5% after Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA missed.

Reuters' BOJ survey shows 86% (61 of 71) of economists expect a December hike, up from 69%. Ueda said hikes will continue, with the Middle East, AI demand and FX as the main risks. The yen is near 160 per dollar.

Australian employment fell 43.5K in October against a +25K consensus, and unemployment rose to 4.9%, a five-year high. Markets priced out further RBA hikes and now expect the first cut in September. RBNZ's Breman flagged inflation warning signs and a December hike is expected.
Japan Tobacco will take a 1.4T yen ($8.9B) charge on writing down its Russian subsidiaries after Moscow's forced seizure.

market_movers.rationale: Anthropic began trading at $111.50 after its IPO priced at $83, closing up 17.1% on the day.
FQ4 revenue light and earnings in line. FY27 guidance brackets the Street and analysts were generally positive on the guide. Stock +10.4%.
FQ1 EPS, revenue and ARR beat. FQ2 guidance above consensus and FY27 outlooks raised. NGS ARR grew 66% y/y. Stock +6.4%.
Q3 EPS, operating income and revenue beat. FY27 revenue and operating income guidance raised. Stock +4.5%.

Fell 7.7% after a Hunterbrook short report alleging a blacklisted Chinese firm kept receiving newer AMD firmware. New US export rules could pressure foreign business. AMD says it complies and called the claims misrepresentations.
FQ4 earnings and revenue better and next-quarter guidance ahead, but management cautioned on limited visibility later in the year. Stock -8.1%.
FQ4 earnings and revenue largely in line and GMV little changed y/y, with lower EMEA volumes and elevated RSCG inventories. Stock -24.9%.
Upgraded to buy at Deutsche Bank on de-risked 2026 guidance, improved earnings profile after the Diatron disposal and recovering core instrument growth.
Sartorius initiated with buy at TD Cowen on expected bioprocess growth near 10% in 2027-28.
Wacker Neuson initiated with hold at Berenberg, citing weak returns and deteriorating H1 2026 indicators.
Michelin downgraded to market perform at Bernstein on H1 2027 cost inflation, weaker pricing power and an expensive valuation.
MFE-MediaForEurope downgraded to hold at Equita on a weak Q4 advertising outlook. Broker cut FY adjusted EBIT estimates by 13% and price targets by about 25%.
Mid-term sales growth guided to 5% a year at constant currency for 2026-2031, narrowed from 5-6% through 2030. Entresto faces generic competition. Stock -3.2%.
McBride warned FY27 adjusted profit would be 20-25% below consensus on petrochemical, energy, packaging and haulage costs. Stock -19.3%.
JD Sports cut FY27 PBT guidance to 700-750M pounds from 700-800M pounds, against prior consensus of 723M. Stock -4.3%.
Tencent fell 6.5% after Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA missed estimates.

earnings_insights: WMT (reported Q3, 11/20 session): modest beat on Q3 and raised FY27 guidance.
PANW (reported FQ1): EPS, revenue and ARR beat. FQ2 guidance above consensus. FY27 revenue, ARR and EPS outlooks raised. NGS ARR +66% y/y.
VVV (reported FQ4): revenue light, earnings in line, FY27 guidance brackets the Street.
P (Everpure, reported Q3): EPS, operating income and revenue beat. Raised FY27 revenue and operating income guidance.
KLIC (reported FQ4): earnings and revenue better than expected, next-quarter guidance ahead of consensus, limited visibility later in the year.
LQDT (reported FQ4): earnings and revenue largely in line, next-quarter guidance brackets consensus.
Soitec (reported H1): EBITDA beat at a 32.5% margin, organic revenue +39%, 2026 free cash flow guidance cut.
Babcock (reported 1H27): EBITA beat consensus by 4%, EBITA +13%, order cover 8.9B pounds, FY27 outlook unchanged.
PORR (reported Q3): EPS 1.14 euros vs 0.89 euros a year earlier. Revenue 1.88B euros vs 1.73B euros estimate. EBIT 65.9M euros in line.
Grainger (reported FY): EPRA EPS 8.1p vs 9.1p estimate. Net rental income 130.2M pounds vs 134.8M pounds estimate.
Tencent (reported Q3): revenue and adjusted EBITDA missed estimates.
Lenovo (reported Q2): revenue $30.2B, above expectations, despite a 21.2% fall in PC shipments on higher component prices.
Japan Tobacco: 1.4T yen ($8.9B) charge on the write-down of its Russian subsidiaries.
Saipem (reported Q3): adjusted EBITDA 468M euros, +7% y/y. FY27 guidance of EBITDA 2B euros and revenue 16.5B euros. Merger with Subsea 7 now targeted for early 2027.
Subsea 7 (reported 3Q26): adjusted EBITDA $549M beat expectations. FY26 revenue guidance raised to about $8B.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lowest since May. New orders were near zero after a fourth straight decline. Both price indexes rose.
Highest since early September. The 4-week average rose 2K to 197,750.
Supports the case for a December ECB hike.
Five-year high. Employment fell 43.5K against a +25K consensus. Markets priced out RBA hikes and moved the first cut to September.

macro_indicators.reading: 86% (61 of 71) expect a hike, up from 69%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus expects a follow-up hike by end-March 2027, taking the policy rate to 1.75%.
Markets price the deposit rate rising from 2.5% to as high as 3.25% next year.

macro_indicators.reading: BoE forecast 4.9%, Bailey expects a lower peak
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market expects a February hike, with some economists still favoring December.

risk_factors: Equity and debt issuance, return on investment and competitive and pricing pressure in AI despite the Anthropic debut.
Debt-heavy neoclouds and lower-tier AI infrastructure may not benefit from IPO demand.
Renewed US strikes on Iran and escalation in the Strait of Hormuz.
Rising odds of a US government shutdown.
AI-linked inflation and tariff-driven inflation that Fed officials say cannot be looked through.
Further US export controls on semiconductors and equipment affecting AMD and ASML.
Energy-driven cost inflation in the UK and Eurozone.
vol_and_positioning: S&P 500 breadth was the worst of the year to date and negative for a fourth straight session.
Possible capital rotation out of megacap AI incumbents into Anthropic shares after tight IPO allocations left institutions underweight.
geopolitical: NY Times reports Trump is weighing another round of extensive strikes on Iran amid new intelligence on Iranian missile, drone and chemical and biological capabilities.
Iran has intensified military activity in the Strait of Hormuz since the midterm elections.
Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral in Shenzhen produced a thin peace declaration that ignored Ukraine.
A bipartisan US bill could extend export restrictions to ASML's DUV immersion tools and support services.
Beijing has linked export controls to EU trade friction, including rare-earths access.
Commission proposes another 45B euros for Ukraine after a 90B euro loan, resting on assumptions about Russian frozen assets.
China and South Korea agreed to expand their FTA to cover services and financials, with preferential treatment for Korean content.
Moscow's forced seizure of Japan Tobacco's Russian subsidiaries.
